title: Near-sunflower analogue of the Erdős-Rado Sunflower Conjecture
statement_text: Let $r \geq 4$. If $\mathcal{F}$ is a $k$-uniform family of sets containing no near-sunflower of size $r$, then $|\mathcal{F}| \leq C^k$, where $C$ is a constant depending only on $r$.
context_text: A family of $r$ distinct sets is a sunflower if all pairwise intersections are equal, i.e. every element belongs to $0$, $1$ or $r$ of the sets; it is a near-sunflower of size $r$ if every element of the ground set belongs to $0$, $1$, $r-1$ or $r$ of the sets (this is interesting only for $r\ge4$, and is invariant under taking complements). A family is $k$-uniform if all its sets have $k$ elements; the ground set is arbitrary. The Erdős–Rado sunflower conjecture asserts that a $k$-uniform family with no sunflower of size $r$ has at most $C_r^k$ members; the best known bound, of Alweiss, Lovett, Wu and Zhang, is $(\log k)^{(1+o(1))k}$, and it applies a fortiori to near-sunflowers. This conjecture is a weaker version of Erdős–Rado. In the setting of subsets of $[n]$ (the Erdős–Szemerédi setting), the authors prove an exponential bound $c^n$ with $c<2$ for near-sunflower-free families, but they could not make progress on this conjecture, even for $r=4$. They prove $|\mathcal{F}|\le2.148^k$ for large $k$ under the stronger condition that $(A\triangle B)\cap(C\triangle D)\ne\emptyset$ for all distinct $A,B,C,D\in\mathcal{F}$. This is extremal set theory rather than graph theory.

title: Informal conjecture on non-tightness of upper bound for binary focal families
statement_text: For $q = 2$ and large $n$, the upper bound $g^{q\text{-ff}}_r(n) \leq (r-1)\, q^{\lceil (r-2)n/(r-1) \rceil}$ (valid for all $q\ge2$ and $r\ge3$) is not tight.
context_text: A family $x^{(0)},x^{(1)},\dots,x^{(r-1)}$ of $r$ distinct vectors in $[q]^n$ is focal with focus $x^{(0)}$ if for every coordinate $i$, at least $r-2$ of the $r-1$ entries $x^{(1)}_i,\dots,x^{(r-1)}_i$ equal $x^{(0)}_i$. $g^{q\text{-ff}}_r(n)$ is the maximum size of a family in $[q]^n$ containing no focal family of size $r$ (for $q=2$, vectors are identified with subsets of $[n]$). The authors prove, for all $q\ge2$ and $r\ge3$, that $c\,\big(q/((q-1)(r-1)+1)^{1/(r-1)}\big)^n\le g^{q\text{-ff}}_r(n)\le(r-1)q^{\lceil(r-2)n/(r-1)\rceil}$ for some constant $c=c(q,r)>0$. When $q\ge n$ is a prime power, a Reed–Solomon-type construction gives $g^{q\text{-ff}}_r(n)\ge q^{\lceil(r-2)n/(r-1)\rceil}$, so the upper bound is tight up to a factor depending on $r$. For $q=2$ the authors believe it is not; as support, they show that for $r=4$ every linear subspace of $\{0,1\}^n$ of dimension at least $0.44n$ ($n$ large) contains a focal family of size $4$, whereas the general upper bound is $3\cdot2^{\lceil2n/3\rceil}$. Focal families are a special kind of near-sunflower (every element lies in $0$, $1$, $r-1$ or $r$ of the sets). This is extremal combinatorics of codes rather than graph theory.
